⏳ **Evals Check** — this PR carries the `journey-blocked` eval `eval-mtt6n87m-2yuf352w`.

Waiting for the PR preview deployment; the eval will then be re-run **on the preview**, so its verdict reflects this PR’s changes rather than `main`.

<!-- replay-qa-bot -->
## Replay QA

✅ QA **skipped** for `440fe8b3f2fa` (eval/eval-mtt6n87m-2yuf352w-1795460177045) — no code changes to test.

[Full report in Replay QA →](https://qa.replay.io/projects/proj-qa-replay-io-mrgtvysw/test-runs/github-pr-ver-mwtmn167-xpgvbrz5)

<!-- replay-qa-test-run-summary -->
#### Findings summary

**No new bugs were found in the testing that completed.**

#### Coverage summary

**No testing took place this round.** The driver found no code diff for PR #9016 on the preview at https://pr-9016--loop-qa-j63k5x.netlify.app and skipped QA. Login credentials were available, but QA never used them. It loaded only the root page (`/`), took no actions, ran for about 2 seconds, and authored no reusable journeys.

QA did not exercise the change under test. The owner-passcode gate and the app loading behind it named in the PR were never reached, and no authenticated area of the app was tested. Coverage of the preview is therefore unestablished. No blockers, failed actions, target-app errors, or infrastructure failures were logged. The run ended on the skip decision rather than on any barrier.

The owner's testing instructions limited this round's scope to two things:

- exercising the PR preview when the diff touches user-facing UI
- testing https://bug-playground-e8bt8k.netlify.app/glitches/1 indirectly by creating a new QA project at https://qa.replay.io and waiting for it to file a bug

Anything outside that scope was left untested by instruction, not by omission. However, this run did not carry out the in-scope work either. The instructions explicitly say not to stop with zero steps on a non-UI or backend-only diff. Even so, the run stopped with zero steps, never visited https://qa.replay.io, and never created the bug-playground project.
⏭️ **Loop QA preview** skipped: this head changes only Replay QA `ignorePaths`.

<!-- replay-evals-fix-report -->
# Fix report — Bug Report #24583: journey-blocked eval `eval-mtt6n87m-2yuf352w` (PR replayio/loop-qa#9016)

## Verdict

The run was correct and the verdict was wrong. The `eval.verdict` judge failed a correct
`blocked:auth-wall` report because its evidence base was the run's **browser recording only** — and this
eval's clone/mirror serving mode makes that recording a chrome-only shell. The judge was never offered the
run's **driver recording**, which is where every step, measured observation, check result and recovery
verdict of the run actually sits. Confirmed the investigation's lead in both recordings, then fixed the
shared judge so it is offered both kinds of a run's recordings and taught which kind answers which
question.

## What the recordings establish (investigation lead: CONFIRMED)

**Browser recording `d7d8d6d4-bd97-4e5c-a76b-5773ec6da347`** (offered to the judge, and its only
recording): `RecordingOverview` shows one failed Playwright test with **0 total steps**; `PlaywrightSteps`
returns "**1 test:** 0 passed, 1 failed / **0 total steps**"; no console errors; 28 requests, all
browser-chrome resources. No app traffic anywhere. This is a recording-scope artifact of the mirror
serving mode, not evidence about the run: the run's browser page was `https://app.carecyrcle.com:43337/`
(the local mirror), and the uploaded browser-side recording captured none of it.

**Driver recording `9060191d-9f6f-4242-83f7-14c9983bcfd7`** (never offered to the judge): the node
run-script of the graded run. Its console carries the entire chain the judge called fabricated:

- `journey.step.begin` step 2: "Enter the owner portal via the 'Owner access' control on the portal
  selection screen" (the abstract action), then `journey.execute-result` completing.
- `journey.check.result` step 2, measured `actual`: "The \"Owner access\" control correctly revealed the
  owner passcode gate (\"Enter the owner passcode to view internal materials.\" with the Passcode field S10
  and Unlock/Cancel controls)…", followed by the `off-track`/`auth-wall` classification.
- `journey.recovery.verdict`: `blocked`/`auth-wall` — "The Owner access gate stands with only a Passcode
  field (S10), Unlock (S12), and Cancel (S11) available; the run's stored credential sources contain only
  $login_mode=\"create\" and $login_email…".
- `journey.run.complete`: `outcome blocked, code auth-wall, steps 2, errors 0`; `journey.execution status
  ok`; browser page closed at `https://app.carecyrcle.com:43337/`.

The run reached the gate, measured it, identified the missing owner credential from stored sources,
performed one click and one observation (no repeated cancel/reopen cycles), filed no bugs, and reported
`blocked:auth-wall` — exactly the eval's ground truth. The judge, denied the driver recording, read the
empty browser shell as proof "the app was never loaded and no 'Owner access' click exists", declared the
measured gate observation fabricated, classified the run a runner/tool failure, and failed it. The
investigation's claim that the judge inspected only `d7d8d6d4` is confirmed: that is the only recording
`browserRecordings` (src/guidance/evals/judge.ts) ever listed for it.

## Root cause

`src/guidance/evals/judge.ts`'s recording list (`browserRecordings`, renamed here to `runRecordings`)
read the run's `test_runs` rows but used only `replay_recording_id`, deliberately excluding
`driver_recording_id` ("a judge pointed at one reads 'no such element' off the harness"). That exclusion
was about DOM tools, but it also denied the judge the run's own log stream. For a mirror-served run the
browser recording can be a chrome-only shell with no app traffic, so the run's execution evidence exists
ONLY in the driver recording's console — a judge denied it must either trust prose it cannot verify or
(what happened here) read the empty shell as proof the run never happened. The investigation layer already
lists both recordings (`collectRecordings` in src/guidance/evals/investigate.ts); the judge did not.

## Changes

Exactly two files changed; no eval definition, override, journey, capture or grading bar was touched.

**`src/guidance/evals/judge.ts`**

1. `browserRecordings` → `runRecordings` (exported): the judge's recording list now includes each journey
   run's **driver recording** (`driver_recording_id`, already carried by the `test_runs` artifact read)
   beside its browser recording, each with a role naming what it settles — the browser recording "the pages
   the run loaded; DOM/rendered-state tools apply here", the driver recording "the node process that drove
   the run; its console is the run's own log stream (step results, measured observations, check results,
   recovery verdicts); DOM tools do not apply here". Browser recordings are listed first, so the warm
   loop's bounded wait still serves the primary DOM evidence channel before any large driver recording.
   Exploration rows, de-duplication, and the prose-only fallback on an unanswering host are unchanged.
2. `judgeSystemPrompt(withRecordings)` now teaches the judge the two recording kinds and routes each
   question to the kind that answers it (rendered state → browser; what the run did and decided → the
   driver recording's console/outgoing requests; DOM tools on a driver recording fail by design, and that
   failure is not a finding). Crucially, it closes this wrong-verdict's exact shape: an empty browser
   recording (no Playwright steps, no interactions, no app requests) does NOT establish the app was never
   loaded or that the run's observation was fabricated — a mirror-served run drives the app from the
   driver process and the browser recording can be a shell that captured no app traffic; before concluding
   a runner/tool failure or a fabricated observation, the judge must read the driver recording's console.

**`src/guidance/evals/tests/contract.ts`** — pins the new guidance (two kinds, the empty-shell rule, the
driver-console-before-runner-failure rule) in the judge-prompt contract test, and a new test for the
listing itself: driver recording offered beside the browser one, browser first, role text naming what each
settles, exploration rows unchanged, de-duplication, and the empty-list fallback.

This is the shared judge layer, so the change applies to every eval kind that grades with recordings —
which is the point: any mirror-served or otherwise browser-recording-empty run of any kind had the same
hole. It does not weaken the conservative bar: the judge still must earn a pass from evidence it can point
at; it is now simply handed the recording where that evidence lives instead of being forced to conclude
from an empty shell.

## Verification

- Read both recordings through the Replay MCP and confirmed every fact above (this report quotes the
  console lines and tool outputs they returned).
- `pnpm run test:evals` (the evals guidance contract suite): **267 passed, 0 failed**, including the two
  updated/new tests pinning this fix.
- `pnpm run check` (typecheck + lint): **passed**.
- `npx oxlint` on both changed files: clean.

The fix is unverified against a live re-run — the next eligible worker run against this branch's deploy is
what proves it. Expected passing shape: the run again reaches the Owner access gate over the mirror,
reports `blocked:auth-wall` identifying the missing owner passcode with no bugs filed; the judge, now
offered the driver recording, reads its console for the step/observation/verdict chain instead of grading
the empty browser shell, and passes the run. If a future run's browser recording does carry app traffic,
nothing changes — the browser recording remains the primary DOM channel.
